memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and hooks, and bronze bases. The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases." - Exodus 27:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every post around the courtyard was made the same way: bronze at the bottom, silver at the top, holding up linen curtains. Nothing was left to chance. Even the fence posts had a specified design, and every one of them was consistent with the others.

Consistency is not a glamorous quality, but it is a godly one. These posts did nothing dramatic. They simply stood, day after day, holding the boundary in place. If a few had been made carelessly or differently, the whole enclosure would have sagged. Their value lay entirely in being reliable and the same.

Much of the Christian life is like that. It is not made of dramatic moments but of ordinary faithfulness repeated over years — showing up, keeping promises, staying honest, praying when you do not feel like it. Paul urges us to stand firm, letting nothing move us, always giving ourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because our labour is not in vain (1 Cor 15:58). You may feel like a fence post rather than a lampstand. But God builds His dwelling with people who simply keep standing where He put them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I faithful in the unglamorous, repeated parts of following Christ?
Where is God asking me simply to keep standing rather than do something dramatic?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, much of following You is ordinary faithfulness rather than dramatic moments. Help me keep standing where You have placed me, steady and reliable, for Your glory. Amen.
